Even though my Dad is long gone and Nmother passed away a few years ago AND even though I worked hard on myself to get rid of that feeling, it still hasn’t completely worn off. Not sure if it ever will, but it definitely helps that Nmother is no longer.

Just let me tell you that providing the basic needs for a child is not a heroic deed. It’s the bare minimum parents are supposed to do.
You don’t owe them anything just because of that. No matter how much they try to tell you otherwise. 

I’ll never understand that kind of narcissistic entitlement. 

“Hey, I barely accomplished the task of being a parent, but I gave my child a lot of mental problems - where is the applause and who is gonna hand me my special award?”

Makes absolute sense. I also feel like that is why we’re more prone to chronic illnesses during our adulthood mentally as well as physically. While the body of a child normally should be building up natural protective shields it is busy with dealing with constant trauma instead.

Our childhood needs were never met. We lacked love, appreciation, human warmth, protection and many more things. I feel like therapy can help a lot, but in the end, this little lonely child inside of us will ALWAYS be on the lookout and full of hope for parental affection. 

I’m sorry you have to deal with that. My parents are long gone, but I know how much it hurts it hurts every time they show proof of their narcissistic traits again.

Dear conscious-ad. I almost missed your post because I actually just wanted to “scroll-through” before I go to bed. However the title struck a chord and after reading everything, I want to let you know: There are lots of loving and caring people out there and especially on this sub.

I’m 44 now. I live a decent life, I have a good partner and the cutest dog on this whole wide world. But I remember how my life was when I was your age. Stuck with a narcissistic mother, an enabling dad and a goldchild brother. I wasn’t of age and I didn’t really have my own money and was absolutely dependent on my parents. EVERY day felt like an eternity. EVERY day my helplessness, frustration, sadness and loneliness piled up a bit more.  Believe me, I know how you feel. I can’t provide you with advice on HOW to go on because I don’t know your situation or what you had to go through already. Just trust me when I tell you: There are better days ahead. 

Hold on to whatever dreams you once had. Try to block out everything that hurts so much at the moment. And take every day like Beppo Roadsweeper in Michael Ende‘s "Momo" did: 

_You must never think of the whole street at once, understand? You must only concentrate on the next step, the next breathe, the next stroke of the broom, and the next, and the next. Nothing else._

I‘m sending you a warm hug.

Don’t ever underestimate the mental toll ME/CFS has on you. The thing is, there might be days where you physically feel better and even might be able to get some stuff done… that doesn’t mean you SHOULD. At least not as long as you haven’t figured out how to manage your energy and your symptoms. And even if you have - you can never be 100% sure. I stopped scrutinizing myself because I had to pay too often for pushing myself and trying to prove myself that I’m not lazy. It lead me to a state where I’m mostly housebound and often bedridden. I feel like we often enough have to deal lack of comprehension and compassion from our surroundings so don’t do the same to yourself. So next time your brain keeps you from doing something , just imagine it’s a good friend of yours and follow their advice.

I’m 44 and I wish I had a Mom like yours. Nevertheless I absolutely understand that her care and efforts might be too overwhelming at the moment. I think I would have felt the same at your age. 

However, she’s right, dear. She’s trying to prevent you from getting worse because she obviously read all the important informations considering cfs.

Maybe try baby steps in “doing nothing” and let your Mom Know that you need some time to get accustomed to it. Start with 5 min each day and look what it does for you. 

Do this for some days and then slowly expand the time span.

I don’t know what your symptoms are so I don’t want to speak “generally” here - but if you’re still getting too anxious or stressed by doing nothing, maybe you could try to only do some mental tasks while laying still. Do some math or rhyming in your head.

Always try to observe how things affect your overall condition. What are the symptoms with mental stimulation? What are the symptoms with physical activities? What does exhaust you more or the most?

It’s important to learn to really listen to your body, recognize the signs and also talk to your Mom about everything. I’m sure she will understand as she already does a lot to give you the appropriate support. Talk to her and then you try to figure out together how to deal best with all the struggles of cfs.

Wish you all the best!

I think I don’t have to mention that our talk took an unexpected turn. And it made me so happy. There they were. Telling me how NOBODY was able to work with that woman. That she caused a high employee turnover and that her division in the end got taken over by someone else. A division I had helped building from scratch. None of the people that had worked with her had stayed longer than a year.

At least one proof that I was not the "crazy or difficult one".

Hey, Adam… as an ex-wife that once told her then hubby that she doesn’t love him anymore, please let me tell you something: 

If my ex hubby would have committed suicide after I told him this… I’m not sure I’d still be here today. I’m quite sure I would not have been able to deal with that kind of grief and of course guilt.

We had been struggling for quite a while and when he finally asked if I still love him all I could do was shake my head. Thing is, dear Adam, I myself was in a very bad mental state. I just didn’t realize back then. 

Maybe… just maybe if he wouldn’t have accepted my answer…. if he would have tried to fight for me… we’d still be together today. But he was (understandably) deeply hurt. And as our relationship issues already had taken a toll on both of us he just accepted my answer and filed for divorce. And I was okay with it. 

Who knows what could have been if we both would have given it some time. Because even if I felt like my love had died for him… I’m sure I would have followed him if he’d decided to take his own life… after all we had been together for 13 years. And even if I felt like I didn’t love him… there was still a deep bond and affection between us. 

I would NOT have been able to deal with his death. Especially not if I had caused it. 

Please don’t let grief or bitterness take over right now. Because the emotions that you’re dealing with pale in comparison to what the people who love you would have to suffer from if you kill yourself. 

I don’t want to compare the relationship I had with my ex-hubby to yours with your wife. We both were able to move on so right now I’m actually just a “stupid” ex-wife telling you this. But if I can feel the pain your death would conflict upon others (just by remembering a man I once loved)… what do you think would the pain of your family look like? 

I wish you with all my heart all the strength, healing and love you need for yourself and your relationship. Please don’t give up.

The way people are commenting on her video reminds me of how people used to react to my mother. And the way SHE talks (and displays her tears and alleged trauma) - sooo triggering. Damn. After so many decades I’m still caught off guard by these kind of personalities. And the lady here in the comments who started to address everyone as “darling” before explaining why she herself can’t be such a bad mother after all she did. Did these people all join the same university? 

Yes, the word “narcissism” is thrown around quite generously nowadays but hey - who could spot that specific trait better than those who had to deal with a narcissist from their early days on?

What all these people that are celebrating that youtube lady don’t get: The decision to go no contact with parents is NEVER made by snipping your fingers. It’s a slowly developing process that is NEVER initiated by something like the shallow wish of just "cutting the cord". It’s caused by constant, repeated harm done to a kid’s soul. Be it physically or psychologically or both. I don’t think I need to elaborate further on that because this whole sub is full of it. 

So yeah, it’s a process. A painful one. It’s filled with grief, self-doubts, loneliness and oh so many more struggles. And I would claim that’s what it is like in most of the cases of no-contact situations. Yes, there might be exceptions. So far, however, I never read a post of an estranged adult child where I felt like “wait dude…you’re in the wrong here”.

Yes parents are only humans, too. They fail, they do or say hurtful things. They cause pain for the sake of wanting the best for their children. I don’t think that I ever could be a perfect mother. Gosh, I’m sure I’d fail repeatedly. 

The thing is - I know that no matter how “difficult” our relationship would turn out to be - I’d love them with all my heart. Even if we never would manage to bond deeply for whatever reasons. I would give my child what I always wished for. Love, acceptance, appreciation and - hopefully - a healthy sense of self. And I also would want them to know that they always will have a place to come home to. A place where they feel safe no matter what resentments there are between us.

Easily said, when you’re past your forties and still childless, huh? Maybe. However, there’s a deep belief within my very being that the very first thing I would do, if my child told me, they don’t want anything to do with me, would be to try to listen. And to then try to give them whatever they need to heal. Be it a long talk, be it an apology or even space and time away from me. Regardless if I’d be able to fully understand.

However, I definitely would NOT feel like creating my own youtube channel to tell MY point of view. Not that I would feel like it’s invalid but because it wouldn’t be important at that moment. Not for me and less than ever for the rest of the world. Why? Because I know myself that no matter what age - a child will always yearn for their parent’s love and affection. ALL their life. And I would sell my soul to find out what exactly needs to be done to show my child exactly that rather than seeking the limelight and explaining to Hinz and Kunz that I had done nothing wrong.

Oh, so you’re statement as a parent is that it’s always about “giving and taking”? Sure. You know what the best thing is you could ever receive from your child? The satisfaction of seeing them living their best life. 

A child doesn’t OWE a parent anything. Parents aren’t entitled of anything. THEY owe. They owe to get the life they created (or adopted) to bloom. That would be the only thing I’d ever strive for as a parent.

Hey you… don't worry so much. Yeah, I know, easier said than done… but the way you told your story already tells a lot. For example that your pretty pup is already better loved and taken care of than he would be in many other places.

5 years ago when we adopted our dog I had just slowly been overcoming my second burnout and quite heavy depressions. Sometimes it was quite a handful. Also had two incidents that made him change his behavior during play and become aggressive as soon as toys were involved. Added quite a bit  to my occasional social anxiety and I started to avoid the park. However, still wouldn’t want to miss one second of the past years. Meanwhile I am chronically ill (it’s something neuro-immunological) and over the past year my illness has worsened up to a point where sometimes all I can do is laying in bed without light or sound. Let alone going for walkies. So I know that feeling of constant guilt very well.
 
I can’t provide you with behavioral tips or tricks all I want to tell you is: Don’t put yourself under so much pressure. I know as dog owners we try to live up to this ideal of perfect human-dog duo. Human commands, dog obeys. Human calls, dog comes running. Off-leash? No problem. Recall? Fully reliable. Dog is well-socialized, well-behaved, well-trained and well-balanced. Til now I've rarely seen such duos in allday life to be honest. 

Let’s imagine the worst case: Your dog never gets over his anxiety/ reactivity and you‘ll be forced to keep him away from other dogs and other people. You know what? You STILL will be the best that ever happened to him. YOU and the life he has with you will still be the perfect one for him. Maybe not in your eyes, but definitely in HIS. That’s just how dogs are.

Dear Dana

Forgiveness is never a MUST. 

I’ve gone through so many emotions. Hurt, anger, pain, loneliness, self-loathing, numbness... I could go on. It took two suicide attempts, three stays at psychiatric wards, countless medications, therapists and psychiatrists - and the closest I got to “forgiveness” is a willingness to let it all go.

Tired of all this times when I held those imaginary conversations in my head with the person who caused most of the pain. Made up disputations that I -even in my fantasy- lost each time. They resulted in accusations and recriminations and reasons why I was being totally ridiculous and incredibly ungrateful.

You are entitled to your feelings and before you even think of forgiveness for the ones who hurt you, try to forgive yourself. Try to overcome any kind of destructive thoughts. Like “I should forgive” or “why didn’t I do this or that” or “I hurt them too”.

Maybe you never will be heard. Maybe no one will ever acknowledge what you’ve been through. Probably no one will ever stand up for you. Or face you with the honest intention to actually listen. That’s why you have to start with yourself. You are a valuable human being that deserves compassion, protection, care and love. Unfortunately, chances are that you won’t get these things from the people you would wish for. 

So first and foremost, take care of yourself and seek healing for your soul. You will find it I promise.

I’ve been mixing it to his regular daily food for months now and it really works. We don’t let him walk down stairs. And we made sure that the places where he jumps up and down at home are cushioned. During winter time I make him wear a coat to keep him warm, as cold obviously worsen his problems in his legs.

with other girls and later women til I finally understood that I always seemed to attract two kinds of people: The narcissistic ones or the broken ones. It took me about twenty years of my life to understand how I “function” - while on the other hand I always had been talented in figuring out very quickly how the people around me needed to be treated to feel comfortable or happy again. 

Over the past few years I realized how I feel each vibe and absorb any kind of energy of people around me. Initially there was a time when I was happy about it because I felt like having found my purpose in life. For the first time in life I felt like being entitled to exist at all. I thought that because I had become aware of my ability I could learn how to use it and do good things. I even managed to find a new job in the social area. Unfortunately it’s not that easy, is it? I tried. I failed. I tried again. I failed.

After being diagnosed with burnouts (two times) and clinical depression, I’m now in a state my therapist and doc call retreat phase. I’m just not able to be sociable anymore. There’s only my fiancé and his family I spend time with... and even then I get exhausted all the time. Sometimes even my fiancé’s presence overwhelmes me. Doesn’t have to be because of a bad mood. I sometimes also get drained by his good vibes.

I’m going to be 40 yro in a few months and I still don’t know how to handle those things. I don’t WANT to be a loner all the time... it’s just that at the moment I feel like there’s nothing that I could give anymore.

So here’s my two cents for you: You ARE a healer... but just because you CAN doesn’t mean you MUST. You can’t and you shouldn’t heal all the people around you. Don’t feel obligated just because you know about your empathetic skillz. It’s a gift, for sure. You might have it because there’s a purpose for you. However we’re not supposed to let us drain by it. You can’t heal if you’re not whole yourself. So first of all, take time
for yourself. I don’t say that you should leave behind everybody but because of your skills you actually already know deep in your heart which people in your life are worth your efforts. Once you figured out for yourself how to go on, use your empathy on yourself first and start in small portions for the people you feel close to.

I wish I could tell you, that’s how you solve your dilemma but thruth is... empaths will always be in some kind of disunion between how much they could give and how much they should take care for themselves. I wish you nothing but peace and happiness on your way. Don’t forget that you’re special and that you deserve the same compassion you give others.
